change.description: Introduce a deployment-owned PostgreSQL schema/role migration ledger, explicit derived-replica bootstrap, separate analytics readiness, and configuration-first rollback for the optional analytics backend.
change.release_unit_description: Managed PostgreSQL analytics migration and cutover design.

planned.reasoning: The existing analytics response contract and SQLite default remain unchanged. The proposal adds durable PostgreSQL migration state and an additive deployment/readiness contract; older releases are not required to read a newly migrated PostgreSQL target and continue on SQLite within the declared rollback window.

scope_drift.description: The implementation extends ADR 0051 beyond its accepted pre-provisioned-schema boundary; ADR 0053, SPEC, implementation notes, and runbook now record the managed startup and online bootstrap contract.

current.reasoning: The implemented state is additive and forward-repairable; startup migration, ledger recording, separate analytics readiness, and online bootstrap orchestration are present, with current-head delivery gates still pending.

public_api.change: planned additive analytics readiness condition or separate readiness endpoint; exact owner choice remains open
public_api.supported_consumer_range: Existing analytics response consumers and SQLite deployments remain unchanged. Deployment consumers must adopt the selected analytics readiness condition before admitting PostgreSQL-dependent traffic.

persistent_state.state_description: PostgreSQL migration ledger, role/schema ownership contract, replica lifecycle, applied-change identities, checkpoints, coverage acknowledgements, and eligibility fences.
persistent_state.source_program_compatibility_range: Existing ADR 0051 deployments remain on the pre-provisioned contract; a future managed-migration release supports the declared additive rollback window and rejects schema/checksum states newer than its reader.

calculation_evidence: Planned and current classifications are provisional until owner decisions, implementation, focused validation, and current-head delivery gates are complete.
